name: step3-holdout-folds
notes: TEMPLATE (neutral). Families are data (${families}, read by one family-availability node, ADR-0226 amendment), so no per-family node exists.  STEP 3 of the three-step data selection (ADR-0222): lock the holdout, admit the feature families, and cut the rolling-origin fold table. Input is step 2's dates file and step 1b's panel (each read back from its upstream onboarding store: dates_root, panel_root, handoff names), the panel read only for each cohort date's settlement_date. Order is the point: (1) holdout-cut locks the last 20% of the cohort's dates and purges dev rows whose label reaches it; (2) a family is admitted (availability node) when available on >= tau (${split.tau}) of dev dates, and the complete-case dates (every admitted family available) are the dates the folds are SIZED by; (3) rolling-origin-plan windows those dates into folds (train_n, val_n, step_n from the plan params, the oldest warmup_folds marked warmup, the rest scored) with the embargo equal to the horizon H (also the DTE the panel rows are selected at). Outputs (the layout): the fold table and the admission-and-metrics file (admitted families, holdout and plan metrics). One document runs ONE ticker (T is the runner's lane); families.flags is the spec of the yes/no columns step 2 wrote and families.dates_fields their file's columns. No training-dates file is written (a writer that runs before the plan could leave a stale file behind a refused run). A fold carries only its boundary dates and counts, and steps 4-6 slice EVERY panel row between those boundaries, so a date missing an admitted family (a few percent of dev dates in the derivation case) is median-imputed there, not excluded, and a fold's train_dates and val_dates count only the complete-case dates, so its window can span more panel dates than the count. Owner decision 2026-10-02 (option A): median imputation is ACCEPTED and no complete-case filter will be built. The knob values are derived in ADR-0222 from the study's committed rows and carried in each node's notes; nothing derivable is typed (embargo, holdout_start, tickers, dates). Selection in steps 4-6 uses warmup folds only and must drop every warm-up validation row whose label reaches plan.scored_start. Memory: the source and the panel are each read once; every other node holds at most one ticker's dates.

step2_dates.notes: Step 2's dates file, read back from step 2's onboarding store (dates_root, handoff): one row per cohort date and ticker with the available_<family> yes/no flags. It carries no DTE or group column: the horizon H is the one DTE of the whole chain. key_fields is (symbol, quote_date) because step 2 refuses a date with two availability patterns, so a duplicate key here means the file was edited. ts_field is quote_date (ISO): these rows carry no asof_ms, and ts_out is free because they carry no such field either.

source.notes: The SAME prepared option panel steps 1-2 read, read here for ONE column step 2's dates.jsonl does not carry: settlement_date, the day each date's label is known (the holdout purge and the embargo need it as end_field). Only dates already in step 2's cohort are looked up from it; no panel row becomes a cohort row. Another panel changes only these params, exactly as in steps 1-2. Root is the onboarding store (source cdf-horizon-panel, stream input_panel), not a per-run copy.

columns.notes: The two column names holdout-cut and rolling-origin-plan must agree on, declared ONCE and referenced by both ($columns.merged.date_field / end_field), so the cut and the folds can never read different dates. date_field is the cohort date (entry day). end_field is settlement_date, the day the label is known: it is the horizon H after the entry date on every row, while expiry can be later on a few rows and would exceed the embargo and refuse (ADR-0222).

tau.notes: tau, the family admission threshold, declared ONCE; the availability node's admit.min_rate reads it ($tau.merged.tau). A family is admitted when it is available on at least tau of the pre-holdout dates. The chosen value and its admitted-family and complete-case counts are recorded in ADR-0222 (flag columns only; aggregate flags are not families); judgment the owner may override. Gaps are assumed random for now, though they may cluster in time.

params.provenance_waiver: each fold row carries its own symbol (the fold_table derive stamps it); the key check proves no ticker appears twice

params.source: The fold table: one row per rolling-origin fold and ticker (fold, role warmup|scored, train/val start and end, date and ISO-week counts, purged), oldest first. Pin it by provenance.sha256 (metrics.sha256) and holdout_start by value; never re-cut it.

fold_evidence.notes: Refuses to overwrite and needs its parent directory: mkdir -p pipeline_runs/step3-holdout-folds, and move that directory aside to repeat. With more than one ticker the file holds one fold-id series per ticker and each ticker has its own holdout_start, so the study's fold_table reader (unique fold ids, one holdout_start) refuses it: for a study, run with ONE foreach key (a copy of this file differing only there) and a fresh output directory.

params.provenance_waiver: each row carries its own symbol; the key check proves no ticker appears twice

params.source: One row per ticker: dev_dates, rate_<f> (share of dev dates on which family f is available), required_<f> (1 = admitted at tau), holdout (holdout-cut metrics: holdout_start, holdout_end, holdout_dates, holdout_weeks, dev_dates, purged_rows, holdout_rows, panel_rows) and plan (rolling-origin-plan metrics: folds, scored, warmup_weeks, scored_start)

admission_evidence.notes: The persisted handoff values: a consumer reads holdout.holdout_start and plan.scored_start BY VALUE from here and never recomputes them (a fraction cut and an end-anchored grid both move when dates are appended). Same overwrite and parent-directory rules as fold_evidence.

foreach.notes: One ticker per run: the study's fold_table reader needs unique fold ids and one holdout_start, so run step 3 once per ticker (set keys to that ticker) into a fresh output directory, then point that ticker's study config at its fold table.

ticker_dates.notes: This ticker's step-2 cohort dates. An empty result (a ticker step 2 never ran) leaves dte without an 'all' key and the run refuses at settled, the first node to read it.

settled.notes: The panel rows at the cohort's DTE whose label is known (step 2's own terminal_return != null rule), kept only to read settlement_date.

settlement_groups.notes: One row per (date, settlement date): expiries on one date collapse here, and a date with two settlement dates yields two rows, which settlement_by_date refuses.

settlement_by_date.notes: quote_date -> settlement_date. A date with two different settlement dates would make its label end ambiguous, so keyby refuses the repeated key.

dated.notes: Adds settlement_date to every cohort date. strict: a cohort date with no panel row at that DTE refuses naming the date, so the source or ticker changing between steps 2 and 3 cannot go unnoticed. This is the only join; step 2's rows lack the column and the kinds need it as end_field.

cut.notes: Holdout FIRST, on the full cohort: the last ceil(0.2 x dates) dates are locked and only dev rows (dates before the holdout whose label settles before holdout_start) and dates-only metrics leave this node. The fraction param sets the holdout size; C4 needs at least 52 weeks, one annual cycle (counts for the derivation case: ADR-0222). Every node after this one reads $cut.records, never $dated, so nothing downstream can see a holdout row.

availability.notes: Replaces the per-family has_/admit_/required_ chains and the rate_ aggregates (ADR-0226 amendment). Reads step 2's yes/no available_<family> columns through flag families (the families spec is data: add or drop a family there, never in the graph) over DEV rows only, because its input is $cut.records. Port 'admission' is the one per-ticker row (dev_dates, rate_<family> = share of dev dates available, required_<family> = 1 when rate >= tau, admitted = sorted names); a rate exactly equal to tau admits. Port 'dates' flags each date complete = every ADMITTED family available. The node refuses a flag column holding anything but yes/no, so a step-2 vocabulary change cannot count as 0. group_keys carry the ticker and selection group so the admission row keeps both.

complete_dates.notes: The complete-case dates: every admitted family available. 'complete' is the availability node's own output field and vocabulary (yes/no), not a project value.

complete_by_date.notes: quote_date -> 'yes' for each complete-case date, as a side table the training join reads. keyby refuses a repeated date, which one ticker's dates never have.

training.notes: Complete-case dates: a dev date stays only when every ADMITTED family is available on it (inner join drops the rest, counted). These dates SIZE and place the folds (the plan counts them); they are not written out and are not a training filter, because steps 4-6 slice by date range and median-impute the dates missing an admitted family. Owner decision 2026-10-02 (option A): median imputation is ACCEPTED and no complete-case filter will be built. Rows keep settlement_date from $cut.records, which the plan needs as end_field.

plan.notes: Count-sized rolling folds over the complete-case dates; all counts are DATES, not weeks. The fold windows are date boundaries that downstream cover ALL cohort dates between them: train_dates and val_dates count only complete-case dates, and the study median-imputes the rest (Owner decision 2026-10-02 (option A): median imputation is ACCEPTED and no complete-case filter will be built). holdout_start and embargo_days are wired (the cut's metric; the horizon H), never typed. val_n, step_n and train_n are chosen so every window meets C2 (>= 8 weeks) and C3 (>= 100 weeks) and C1 (>= 10 scored folds) holds; the derivation case is in ADR-0222. warmup_folds is the smallest k meeting C5 (warm-up validation spans >= 52 ISO weeks, every season once) that still leaves C1; ADR-0222 records the sweep over k (weeks spanned vs scored folds left). All selection (steps 4-6) runs on role == warmup only; scored folds are the clean evidence. The plan refuses a row on or past holdout_start and a label longer than the embargo, and a ticker with too few dates yields no fold and refuses. PROVISIONAL: these values were derived on one case's step 2 rows and must be re-derived, not merely re-tested, when step 2 is rebuilt or another ticker is added.

fold_table.notes: Stamps the ticker on each fold row so several tickers can share one file. The plan's own columns are untouched, so the rows are exactly what the node emits.

protocol_holdout.notes: Attaches the holdout-cut metrics (dates and row counts only: holdout_start, holdout_end, holdout_dates, holdout_weeks, dev_dates, purged_rows, holdout_rows, panel_rows) to the admission row.

protocol.notes: Attaches the plan metrics (folds, scored, warmup_weeks, scored_start). The result is the single per-ticker row admission_evidence writes: the admitted families next to the two seams a consumer pins by value.
